title: No non-closed point in the distinguished fibre
statement: Let S be a scheme, Ω an algebraically closed field, s : Spec Ω → S a geometric point, A a commutative local ring, and e : Spec A ≅ S_(s), where S_(s) is [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] and its structural map ρ_s is [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. For every x in Spec A, if ρ_s(e(x)) = s(closedPoint Ω), then x = closedPoint A.

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood Spec R of the image p of s and factor s through it. The affine pointed-neighbourhood/triple equivalence, its initial chart restriction, and the small-model comparison identify the colimit C defining S_(s) with the etale residue-triple colimit. These comparisons preserve the structural R-map on every coprojection. The selected residue field is the relative separable closure of κ(p) in Ω; pointed etale residue extensions land there because they are finite separable.

The triple theorem gives a local colimit with maximal ideal pC. The prime corresponding to e(x) contracts to p, so it contains pC and equals that maximal ideal. Thus e(x) is the closed point of Spec C. The inverse isomorphism preserves closed singletons, and Spec A has a unique closed point. Hence x is closedPoint A. This also works when A is a field; a zero ring A cannot admit e since C has a field quotient.

    (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) (e : Spec (.of A) ≅ strictHenselizationScheme s)
    (x : Spec (.of A))
    (h : (e.hom ≫ strictHenselizationStructuralMap s) x =
      s (IsLocalRing.closedPoint Ω)) :
    x = IsLocalRing.closedPoint A
